horizontal.initial:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a production pixel-art animation sprite sheet for a Japanese children's multiplication learning game. Reference image is ONLY for character identity: cheerful young samurai, dark navy ponytail with teal tie, blue and teal short kimono with gold edging, navy trousers, orange scarf, sandals, silver katana. Translate to charming readable 16-bit game pixel art with crisp square pixels, limited palette, no antialiasing. Actual transparent background.
EXACT layout: square 1024x1024 PNG, precisely 4 columns x 2 rows, eight equal 256x512 cells, no margins or gaps. Read in row-major order. Each frame contains ONE full-body samurai and its compact blade trail only, fully inside the cell with generous transparent padding, consistent character scale, consistent centered root anchor, no grid lines, no lettering, no numbers, no environment, no diagram, no drop shadow background.
This sheet is HORIZONTAL LEFT-TO-RIGHT DASH SLASH. Samurai faces screen RIGHT in clear side view in every frame. Orange scarf and ponytail stream LEFT. The game will move the entire sprite rightward; keep the character centered in each cell rather than moving across the sheet.
Eight chronological frames: 1 crouch with sheathed blade preparing; 2 draw sword leaning right; 3 powerful rightward launch; 4 full speed slash with a narrow white/cyan horizontal cutting trail aligned across waist height, 5 strongest forward slash and short trailing horizontal streak LEFT of body, 6 follow-through with blade extended right, 7 braking low stance, 8 composed finishing pose. The blade cut direction must read horizontal left-to-right. Keep effects compact and the character unobscured so the underlying math diagram remains visible. Friendly heroic, no enemies, no violence against people, no blood. Entire weapons and scarf must be within each cell. Sheet should look like actual usable game frames, not illustrations or a poster.
horizontal.spacingRevision:
Use case: stylized-concept. EDIT the supplied HORIZONTAL samurai pixel-art sprite sheet into a safely spaced usable sprite atlas. Preserve the same eight chronological poses, character identity, costume and crisp pixel art. Preserve real transparent background.
CRITICAL CHANGE: shrink EACH samurai plus ALL its sword/scarf/slash effects to fit entirely within the CENTRAL 65 PERCENT of its own cell. Use an exact regular 4-column by 2-row layout. All eight cells equal, row-major. Leave a LARGE transparent moat around EVERY frame on ALL four sides. Nothing at all should touch image edges or neighboring sprites. The white/cyan slash effects in frames 4 and 5 and extended sword in frame 6 MUST be shortened to fit their own cell. Each character's body root must be at the SAME location relative to each cell. Do not draw grid lines or labels.
Horizontal left-to-right dash: face RIGHT, scarf streams LEFT, blade/trail aligned horizontal. Eight poses: anticipation, draw, launch, slash, strongest slash, follow-through, brake, finish. No additional frames, no extra objects, no lettering. This is a technical sprite sheet, not a showcase illustration. Output a wide canvas with four equal columns and two equal rows; generous blank alpha padding is more important than making large sprites.

vertical.initial:
Use case: stylized-concept. Make the VERTICAL DOWNWARD DASH SLASH companion sprite sheet to the reference horizontal pixel-art samurai sprite sheet. Reference is character/style identity, NOT an edit target. Same cheerful chibi young samurai with dark navy ponytail, teal hair tie, blue/teal gold-edged kimono, orange scarf, navy pants, sandals, silver katana, same crisp 16-bit pixel-art style.
Transparent background. EXACTLY eight frames, arranged in 4 equal columns and 2 equal rows, row-major order. Each sprite completely INSIDE its own equal rectangular cell with at least 12% empty padding on ALL sides including weapon/trail/scarf. Absolutely no part may enter another cell. NO labels, numbers, borders, grid, ground, backdrop or text. Consistent scale and center anchor for body. This is an actual game sprite sheet.
Dedicated vertical animation, NOT a rotated horizontal sprite. Camera is a readable front three-quarter view facing DOWN towards the bottom edge of the screen, so child can see face. Movement goes from screen TOP to screen BOTTOM. Scarf and ponytail trail UPWARDS, motion streaks vertical. Blade cuts a very narrow VERTICAL line through the center, never a broad horizontal slash.
Frames 1 through 8: 1 poised high with sword raised above head; 2 bend knees both hands lifting sword overhead; 3 launching downwards, feet tucked, blade begins to descend; 4 strong overhead-to-downward sword stroke, compact bright silver/cyan VERTICAL trail in front of body; 5 strongest straight DOWN cut, long thin vertical silver blade aimed at bottom of cell, scarf points up; 6 downward follow-through, blade remains aligned DOWN; 7 braking low with blade lowered; 8 calm finishing stance with blade down and face readable. The whole sprite itself stays centered in each cell because game code will translate it down the math diagram. Friendly heroic children's game. No blood, enemies or targets. Preserve compact pixels and palette from reference, no smooth painting or photorealism. ALL eight full characters and all effects must have ample isolated transparent padding, no touching neighboring frames.
vertical.spacingRevision: Use case: stylized-concept. EDIT supplied vertical-downward samurai pixel-art sprite sheet into a safely spaced usable game sprite atlas. Preserve EXACT same eight chronological poses, identity, costume, and crisp pixel style. Preserve actual transparent background. CRITICAL CHANGE: shrink EACH whole sprite including sword, scarf and all cyan effects to fit within CENTRAL 65 PERCENT of each cell. Exact regular 4 columns x 2 rows of EQUAL cells, row-major. Large TRANSPARENT padding on ALL four sides of EVERY frame. Same character scale and centered body root relative to each cell. No sprites or effects may touch canvas edges or any neighboring frame. No grid lines, labels or text. Vertical top-to-bottom movement, camera front three-quarter with face visible, scarf points UP, blade cuts DOWN. Do NOT rotate the sheet or the character sideways. Keep the katana and cyan trail thin and VERTICAL. Eight frames: raised sword, anticipation, downward launch, downward slash, strongest downward slash, follow-through, braking, finishing. Technical isolated sprite sheet, ample empty alpha is more important than large sprites.
